stories.body: G7 leaders agreed to a coordinated release of 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from emergency reserves over four months, including a substantial diesel release within the first 20 days, in an effort to curb surging energy prices. The move follows disruption to Gulf exports during the US-Israel war with Iran, attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, and damage to Russian energy infrastructure in the Ukraine war. The group also pledged not to impose energy-export restrictions among its members after President Donald Trump had threatened to ban US diesel exports unless Europe released more of its reserves. Separately, the UK maritime agency reported that two oil tankers had been hit by unidentified projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.headline: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel as Hormuz attacks disrupt supplies

stories.body: Brazilian voters go to the polls Sunday in a closely fought presidential election between the 80-year-old leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, seeking a fourth nonconsecutive term, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the far-right son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro. Polls put the candidates in a statistical tie, with one recent Datafolha runoff simulation giving Lula 47 percent to Bolsonaro's 45 percent. The race is seen as consequential for Latin America's political alignment: Bolsonaro has promised closer alignment with Donald Trump's regional agenda, while Lula has criticized US intervention and stressed regional sovereignty. Analysts say the Bolsonaro family's durable appeal rests not only on its core supporters but also on longstanding anti-Workers' Party sentiment.
stories.headline: Brazil prepares for a tight presidential contest between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro

stories.body: A Russian attack damaged the road surface and trolleybus wires on Kyiv's Northern Bridge, temporarily blocking traffic across another vital crossing of the Dnipro River, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The strike followed repeated drone attacks on the Southern Bridge, where metro and car traffic have been suspended, and marks an escalation in attacks on infrastructure connecting the capital's eastern and western banks. Russia said the bridge was used for military logistics, while Ukrainian officials warned that strikes on bridges, power facilities, hospitals, schools and communications networks are making life in the city increasingly untenable. Kyiv faces a shortage of Patriot interceptors as Russia deploys faster jet-powered drones and intensifies its campaign ahead of winter.
stories.headline: Russia strikes a second major bridge across Kyiv's Dnipro River

stories.body: The United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said a Flydubai co-pilot used a cockpit crash axe to attack the captain and tried to seize control of an Israel-bound flight from Dubai, describing the incident as an attempted terrorist act. The aircraft, carrying more than 170 passengers, plunged about 17,000 feet before the injured captain opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to subdue the co-pilot; reserve pilots then diverted and landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia. Investigators are examining the suspect's motives and possible links, while reports say he was an Omani national previously removed from flying duties at Oman Air over concerns about extremist views. The captain was hospitalized and reported to be in stable condition.
stories.headline: UAE calls Flydubai cockpit attack an alleged terrorist act

stories.body: North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile from the eastern port city of Wonsan into the Sea of Japan, South Korea's military said, adding that it travelled more than 700 kilometres. Seoul convened an emergency national-security meeting, heightened surveillance for further launches and said it would share intelligence with the United States and Japan; US Pacific Command said the launch posed no immediate threat to US territory or allied personnel. The test came a day after Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, rejected South Korean demands for an apology over landmine explosions in the demilitarized zone that seriously injured three South Korean soldiers and warned Pyongyang was ready for any response.
stories.headline: North Korea launches ballistic missile amid renewed tensions with Seoul

stories.body: Rebels from Ethiopia's Tigray People's Liberation Front were reportedly abandoning Mekelle, the regional capital, as federal forces and pro-government militias advanced. Fighting has intensified since September 23, with the TPLF also launching attacks into neighbouring regions, raising fears of a renewed nationwide conflict similar to the 2020-22 civil war. The reported retreat comes amid wider regional tension after Ethiopia and Eritrea severed ties, while the African Union has urged all sides to show restraint.
stories.headline: Tigray rebels reportedly leave Mekelle as Ethiopian forces advance

stories.body: The World Health Organization warned that repeated delays in allowing medicines, prosthetics and other medical supplies into Gaza could have devastating consequences for Palestinians who need urgent care. Its representative in Palestine said aid is currently limited largely to the Kerem Shalom crossing, while other main entry points remain closed and Rafah permits only restricted movement of people, including patients seeking treatment abroad. The agency said one shipment of prosthetics and assistive devices had been rejected four times in six months, while winter, unsafe shelter, poor sanitation, lack of clean water and rising disease risks are compounding the crisis. The warning came as an Israeli strike on a residential apartment in Gaza City's densely populated Remal neighbourhood reportedly killed at least five people.
stories.headline: WHO warns that delayed medical aid could have devastating consequences in Gaza

stories.body: The US economy added 29,000 jobs in September, missing expectations, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2 percent and wage growth continued to lag inflation. The government's final employment report before the November 3 midterm election presents another economic challenge for President Donald Trump and Republican candidates, with voters confronting higher living costs.
stories.headline: US jobs growth disappoints as unemployment rises to 4.2 percent before midterms

stories.body: New York Governor Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in a 2024 gang-rape allegation involving a former Cornell student and called for legislation to close what she described as a loophole in state sexual-assault law involving voluntary intoxication. The former student says she was coerced into taking drugs and raped at a fraternity house; Hochul criticized Cornell police for allegedly failing to provide the local district attorney with the full account and faulted the prosecutor for declining charges without interviewing the complainant. Cornell backed the appointment and said it would conduct an independent external review, while the district attorney said his office had not been given the full picture.
stories.headline: New York appoints special prosecutor in Cornell rape case and seeks to change intoxication-consent law

stories.body: The Senate Leadership Fund, the leading Republican Senate super PAC, has reserved more than $8 million in Kansas advertising to defend Senator Roger Marshall while pausing future spending in North Carolina, where it had already spent more than $30 million supporting Republican Michael Whatley. Private polling reportedly shows Marshall in a dead heat with Democrat Adam Hamilton in a state Republicans have dominated for decades, while former North Carolina governor Roy Cooper continues to lead Whatley in polls. Republican operatives cite the political damage from high diesel and fertilizer prices, tariffs, the Iran war and immigration enforcement, particularly in agriculture-heavy Midwestern states, as they are forced to defend seats that had not been expected to be competitive.
stories.headline: Republicans shift Senate resources from North Carolina to unexpectedly close Kansas race

stories.body: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is considering whether to call an early election after Congress rejected two government housing decrees with votes from Junts, the Popular Party and Vox. Sánchez had urged lawmakers to support measures including an eviction moratorium and lease protections, warning that history would judge those blocking them, a remark widely interpreted as a signal that an election could come soon. Although officials said no final decision had been made, allies in the government and Socialist Party see the housing crisis, public anger over recent evictions and growing left-wing mobilization as a possible opening before inflation and parliamentary instability worsen.
stories.headline: Sánchez weighs early election after Congress defeats housing decrees

stories.body: Housing activists held demonstrations in Madrid, Barcelona and cities across Spain after Congress rejected the government's housing decrees, while encampments continued in Madrid's Puerta del Sol and Barcelona's Plaça de Catalunya. Protesters demanded access to affordable housing, stronger tenant protections and a general strike, with marches planned or under way in more than 20 cities despite rain. The movement gained momentum after the eviction of an elderly Madrid resident known as Maricarmen, whose case became a symbol of the crisis, and organizers said the parliamentary defeat had intensified rather than ended their campaign.
stories.headline: Housing protests spread across Spain after Congress rejects emergency measures

stories.body: Torrential rain flooded the town of Madrigueras in Albacete, killing a 102-year-old woman after water inside her home rose above one metre and forcing emergency crews to rescue about 90 people. The town recorded 142 litres of rain per square metre, prompting the regional government to activate its adverse-weather emergency plan. Firefighters, Civil Guard officers, police, Civil Protection volunteers and the Red Cross were deployed for rescues, cleanup and vehicle removal; the local health centre was flooded and its services were moved to a Red Cross facility.
stories.headline: Severe flooding in Albacete kills a 102-year-old woman and prompts 90 rescues

stories.body: Two Moroccan migrants told El País they were returned from Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta against their will without being offered an opportunity to seek international protection or having their information and fingerprints taken. The men, aged 22 and 25, had lived in informal settlements at Benítez beach since a mass entry into Ceuta in late July and believed police were taking them to temporary reception centres. Instead, they said a police translator told them the decision to return them had already been made, after which they were transferred to Moroccan authorities and taken hundreds of kilometres from the border.
stories.headline: Moroccan migrants say they were forcibly returned from Ceuta without access to asylum procedures

stories.body: Catalonia's weather service issued its highest-level warnings for torrential rain in Barcelona and parts of the coast and pre-coast, with forecasts of more than 40 litres per square metre in 30 minutes and potentially more than 90 litres in three hours. The most dangerous period was expected overnight into Sunday, when a Mediterranean low-pressure system could bring localized totals of 100 to 200 litres per square metre, particularly in Barcelona and Girona provinces. Civil Protection kept the Inuncat flood plan on alert and urged residents to avoid basements and garages, monitor official warnings and take precautions near rivers, streams and flood-prone areas.
stories.headline: Catalonia issues highest rain warnings for Barcelona and surrounding coastal areas

stories.body: Barcelona housing groups called for a general strike after Congress struck down the Spanish government's housing decrees, as activists maintained an encampment in Plaça de Catalunya and blocked sections of Gran Via and Avinguda Meridiana. The Sindicat de Llogateres said it was speaking with CCOO, UGT and CGT about organizing a strike in coming months, arguing that a broader mass movement was needed to transform the housing system. An open assembly in Plaça de Catalunya backed the idea but did not set a date, while organizers urged sustained mobilization over evictions, high rents, speculation and shortages of affordable public housing.
stories.headline: Barcelona housing activists call for a general strike after defeat of housing decrees
